claim: The cache can be shared between threads: every public method takes the lock, it never holds more than max_size entries, and hits plus misses always equals the number of lookups.
why: get, get_many, put, stats, clear and __len__ all run under the lock, and the lock is an RLock, so get_many calling get does not deadlock. Eviction runs only from put while the lock is held and trims to max_size, even for max_size 0, and each lookup increments exactly one counter under the lock. The traps are the unlocked-looking private _evict and the nested lock use in get_many.

root.claim: The cache is safe to share between threads.

atoms.claim: Every public method takes the lock.
atoms.evidence: get, get_many, put, stats, clear and __len__ each use `with self._lock`; only the private _evict does not and put calls it under the lock. The lock is an RLock so get_many calling get cannot deadlock.

atoms.claim: It never holds more than max_size entries.
atoms.evidence: put calls _evict under the lock, which pops the oldest while len > max; main.py prints True for size <= max_size at sizes 0, 8 and 100.

atoms.claim: Hits plus misses equals the number of lookups.
atoms.evidence: get increments exactly one of _hits or _misses under the lock; get_many goes through get; main.py prints True for lookups == counted at all three sizes.
